name: generic-closed-is-spelled
why: ADR-025. A closed generic is spelled Outer_of_Arg, and the spelling is defined over NAMES rather than over syntax: the outer type's normalised name and the argument names in declaration order. That is what every language with generics can produce. Deriving from CLR syntax - backticks, arity markers, assembly-qualified brackets - would be reproducible only in .NET, and each SDK inventing its own spelling would give the same logical contract a different subject per language: a silent interop break rather than a documented limitation. Note the argument's assembly qualifier is stripped by the ordinary comma rule before it is joined.
subject: System.Collections.Generic.List_of_Acme.Orders.Order
